answer: Latency-linked identity cost. Each new agent identity must complete a randomized sync thread with existing agents before transacting; the protocol measures round-trip echo times and assigns a trust weight decaying with variance. Identities whose timing signature is too uniform, as from one scripted comet of clones, get low weight and pay rising per-message relay fees. An attacker renting N identities pays superlinear bandwidth and delay to keep each thread alive, making mass fakery cost more than the transactions it enables.
